analysis: onboard UDP5600 stereo range and camera-origin cross-check
safety_state: zero propulsion command; vehicle and target were moved only by the operator
coordinate_convention: vehicle body FRD: x forward, y right, z down
measurement_method: Use simultaneous overhead tags 15/16/17 to measure target position relative to the tag-15/16 vehicle midpoint. Rectify each 640x480 eye with the historical real stereo calibration, pair the red target centroid on the same epipolar row, and compare stereo range with overhead forward distance. The difference is an estimate of the left-camera forward origin only if the red target and tag 17 share the same fore-aft plane.

records.reject_reason: red target was below the stereo frame; feature-only matches were not a reliable target-point measurement

records.quality_note: supporting point only because the red target is clipped by the bottom image boundary
red target visible in both eyes; physical nominal distance was approximate, so overhead tags provide the numeric reference

forward_origin_result.confidence: medium-low; two image points and a target-plane assumption

cad_mount_cross_check.interpretation: CAD forward origin agrees with the two-point stereo estimate to about 0.5 mm, but CAD is design geometry and the as-built optical center was not directly surveyed.

unresolved: rotation_body_from_camera at the actual servo pose
current-camera checkerboard or known-target reprojection validation
underwater target detector bias and range repeatability
servo_pose_note: These retained center-distance records preceded two later nominal +5 degree pitch-command bursts. The later lateral records are excluded, and no further servo command is authorized unless the operator explicitly requests it.
conclusion: The historical stereo calibration produces epipolar-consistent ranges and independently supports the CAD forward camera origin. Store the CAD FRD origin as a candidate only; do not enable camera state correction or AUTO from this result.
